reviews.quote: No professional review found for this line as of 2026-11; ratings inferred from specs and sibling-line reviews.

praises: 1TB SSD at $949.97 — double the storage of most rivals at this price
i7-1355U's 10 cores chew through office multitasking; snappiest Intel office CPU of the HP group
Dual 8GB DDR4 SO-DIMMs: proper dual-channel and an upgrade path to 32GB
SD card reader built in — handy for photographers on a budget
Jet Black finish and micro-edge display look professional in a meeting room
complaints: USB-C is explicitly data-only per HP's own spec — no charging, no monitor
Panel type unstated and almost certainly a TN: dim, off-axis colour washout
720p webcam and average speakers; McAfee + Microsoft 365 trial bloat on first boot
Modest ~41 Wh battery gives ~5h, not the claimed 7h, under real loads

standouts: 1TB NVMe + 16GB dual-channel DDR4 in a 10-core Intel for under $950 — storage-per-dollar leader of the HP group
design_philosophy: HP's spec-sheet special: the storage and CPU numbers do the selling — i7 badge, 1TB, 16GB dual-channel — while the invisible parts (a probably-TN 250-nit panel, a data-only USB-C, no backlight, small battery) absorb the cost. It rewards buyers who shop on numbers and punishes those who care about the display.
